name: TenantCloud
description: TenantCloud is property-management software for landlords and property managers. Property teams use it to manage properties, units, leases, tenants, owners, rent collection, payments, maintenance requests, rental applications, tenant screening, accounting, listings, websites, reports, lead tracking, team roles, and owner and tenant portals.
agentUseSummary: TenantCloud cannot yet be connected through Relay as a direct self-service provider. TenantCloud publishes a GraphQL API endpoint and personal access token flow, but its public documentation says the schema file is currently available only through live introspection, so Relay cannot safely expose a raw GraphQL surface or infer a bounded property-management contract without an authorized scoped token and frozen schema.

blocked.label: Connect TenantCloud
blocked.description: TenantCloud documents personal access tokens and a GraphQL endpoint, but Relay has no approved static schema, operation list, scope matrix, tenant binding, revocation, or acceptance contract to implement.

blocked.label: Read TenantCloud records
blocked.description: Properties, units, leases, tenants, owners, applicants, screenings, rent, payments, maintenance, accounting, listings, reports, lead tracking, team settings, portals, documents, and communications remain unavailable to Relay.

blocked.label: Change TenantCloud records
blocked.description: Creating, updating, importing, exporting, posting, charging, paying, reconciling, messaging, assigning, archiving, deleting, or otherwise changing property-management records is blocked.

blocked.label: Operate payments or accounting
blocked.description: Rent collection, online payments, deposits, owner distributions, ledgers, accounting entries, bank data, reconciliations, invoices, fees, balances, statements, and financial reports are blocked.

blocked.label: Run raw GraphQL
blocked.description: Arbitrary GraphQL queries, mutations, introspection, custom operation text, and schema exploration are blocked until product and security approve a frozen typed operation contract.

blocked.label: Use private TenantCloud access
blocked.description: Browser automation, session cookies, user passwords, private APIs, traffic inspection, screen scraping, unofficial endpoints, and provider-console activity are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No TenantCloud action is enabled until Relay has an authorized least-privilege TenantCloud token, a frozen introspected schema, exact allowed operations, data categories, scope requirements, legal constraints, audit behavior, retention, revocation, and disconnect handling.

runtimeSupport.description: No TenantCloud tools are mounted until an authorized scoped PAT, frozen schema, and bounded property-management operation contract are approved.
No TenantCloud tools are mounted until an authorized scoped PAT, frozen schema, and bounded property-management operation contract are approved.

providerSetup.blocker: TenantCloud publishes API documentation for a GraphQL endpoint at https://api.tenantcloud.com/graphql and says users create personal access tokens with scopes in the TenantCloud web app, with the token secret shown once. The public GraphQL documentation also says the schema file is currently available only through introspection. Relay cannot mount raw arbitrary GraphQL or derive safe property-management tools from a live account without an authorized representative token, frozen schema, exact operation list, scope matrix, tenant and portfolio binding, version strategy, privacy/legal review, and data-governance contract for sensitive housing, tenant, owner, payment, accounting, maintenance, communication, and screening records.
providerSetup.nextAction: Product, security, privacy, legal, property-management, payments/accounting, housing-compliance, tenant-data, and provider-console owners must approve a TenantCloud implementation plan. An authorized TenantCloud administrator should create a dedicated least-privilege user and PAT with exact scopes in the provider-console task, introspect the schema without exposing secrets in Git, freeze versioned typed queries and mutations, define readable fields, write authority, payments/accounting exclusions, fair-housing and screening constraints, audit, retention, redaction, revocation, deletion, and disconnect behavior, then complete live acceptance before Relay enables TenantCloud actions.

evidence.supports: TenantCloud publishes API getting-started documentation, including a personal access token workflow from the TenantCloud web app, scoped token creation, one-time token-secret display, and bearer-token request examples.

TenantCloud documents its API as mostly GraphQL with endpoint https://api.tenantcloud.com/graphql, recommends POST for mutations, and says schema introspection is currently the way to obtain the schema file.
TenantCloud documents API version selection through a Version header and warns that omitting it defaults to latest, which is unstable and may include breaking changes.

TenantCloud describes property-management capabilities for rent collection, maintenance, accounting, rental applications, tenant screening, listings, leases, reports, lead tracking, team roles, and owner and tenant portals.
TenantCloud terms govern use of the service and place responsibility on users for housing, privacy, anti-discrimination, and other legal compliance while prohibiting unauthorized access and misuse.
TenantCloud publishes a privacy policy covering personal information processed through its websites, applications, and services.
